main_claim: AtlasLift is reference-qualified and endpoint-specific: reference recovery, selector choice and functional geometry lift are separate tests.

panels.A: Cross-dataset held-unit/global geometry, emphasizing WARP positive, McLachlan exact positive, and Bugeon/Shainer/Condylis boundaries.
panels.B: McLachlan same-K reference × selector interaction; exact PERI/ECT supports function-guided geometry at K20/K23, but broad references can win under atlas-variance selection.
panels.C: Xu PVN target-free C185 bridge recovers masked genes (median rho~0.244) but strict held-mouse external-gene endpoint lift is not supported.
panels.D: Bugeon exact VISp boundary: exact reference qualification does not imply significant global held-mouse geometry lift.

guardrails: Do not infer exact-region reference superiority from McLachlan; reference × K × selector interact.
Conditional random-panel P/q are not small-n animal exchangeability P values.
Xu measured-gene recovery and downstream functional endpoint lift are separate claims.
Do not turn endpoint-specific atlas positives into a universal global-geometry claim.
